Meanwhile most modern applications rely on a cache to shrink latency between users and distant databases; a well-tuned cache absorbs repeated reads, letting only fresh writes travel further, so throughput rises even as request volume grows across busy service tiers.

However caching strategies vary across teams; some choose write-through caches that save every update at once, while others favor write-back caches that batch changes for a later flush, trading durability for speed. Choosing a sound eviction policy matters just as much, since a poor policy can quietly erase gains that developers worked hard to build.

Along this track, an app avoids slow disk trips and pulls input from a quick local stash, cutting lag and costs. A small stash holds hot bits, not all facts, so odds of a miss stay low, and load stays calm.

Finally teams should monitor cache hit rates continuously; small tuning adjustments compound over months, and the migration work is done.
